item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Sharif’s 2024 record is mixed but leans negative on 3B.6. There is real evidence of counterterrorism mobilization and repeated calls for dialogue, but the dominant pattern is coercive: election shutdowns, political policing, mass arrests, minority-targeted enforcement, and weakening of judicial checks. I found no strong evidence of a sustained strategy to reduce fear without expanding the political fear climate. Confidence: moderate.

**Accepted Items**
- [PM for collective efforts to eliminate menace of terrorism](https://www.radio.gov.pk/22-06-2024/pm-for-collective-efforts-to-eliminate-menace-of-terrorism) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-06-22  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif launched a national counterterrorism campaign with provincial consensus and said the armed forces would be supported with necessary resources. This is the clearest pro-reduction item, because it addresses a real violent threat through formal, collective authority.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- [Peace in South Asia depends on settlement of Kashmir dispute](https://www.radio.gov.pk/21-09-2024/peace-in-south-asia-depends-on-settlement-of-kashmir-dispute-pm) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-21  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif publicly framed security in terms of dialogue and peaceful settlement. This supports a de-escalatory posture, though it does not by itself show a broader domestic fear-reduction strategy.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- [PM urges UN to take action against Israel's genocidal acts](https://www.radio.gov.pk/26-09-2024/pm-urges-un-to-take-action-against-israels-genocidal-acts) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-26  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif urged confidence-building measures to prevent war and reduce tensions. This is the strongest public de-escalation language in the record.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- [Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on peoples' rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty condemned the telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation. This is direct evidence of coercive administrative control that likely increased, rather than reduced, public fear.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- [Pakistan government intensifies crackdown on political dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09  
  Claim-level summary: HRW reported over 500 arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, mobile internet cuts, and arrests for peaceful protest. This is strong evidence that the state used force in ways that generated a broader political fear climate.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- [Pakistani police detain two parliamentarians in swoop on ex-PM Khan's party](https://theprint.in/world/pakistani-police-detain-two-parliamentarians-in-swoop-on-ex-pm-khans-party/2260202/) | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-10  
  Claim-level summary: Police detained PTI parliamentarians after a rally demanding Khan’s release. This supports a pattern of intimidation rather than fear reduction.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- [Pakistan authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and orders blocking Ahmadi rites. That is direct evidence that state and local authorities were not reducing communal insecurity and were instead reinforcing it.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- [Pakistan's government curbs judiciary's power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | The Guardian | 2024-10-21  
  Claim-level summary: Critics said the 26th amendment reduced judicial independence amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. That undercuts any claim that Sharif was creating a safer, less fearful political order.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.4`, `3B.5`

- [2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html) | U.S. Department of State | 2024  
  Claim-level summary: The report says the government rarely took credible steps to identify and punish officials who committed abuses. This suggests fear and abuse were not being systematically reduced through accountable institutions.  
  Question IDs: `3B.6`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`

**Search Gap**
I did not find evidence of a durable, Sharif-led domestic fear-reduction program that paired security policy with strong protections against political intimidation, communal abuse, or abusive policing. The best positive items are reactive counterterrorism and diplomatic de-escalation; the broader 2024 record remains dominated by coercive controls and a heightened fear climate.
